fieldMarks: Large, long-tailed game bird, 76-91 cm including the tail.
Male: colourful and iridescent with a long pointed tail and a white neck ring.
Female: mottled brown with a long tail and pale belly.
The darker 'green pheasant' form found locally on the east coast has males without the white neck ring.
behavior: Male territorial call is a loud crowing 'caw-cawk!' followed by a resonant beating of the wings; flushes with a loud cackle.
Winter flocks are often segregated: small groups of males and larger flocks of females.
Feeds on the ground by scratching and digging; omnivorous, eating grain, seeds, green shoots, berries and insects.
habitat: Semi-open habitat: farmland with mixed crops, brushy meadows, hedgerows, woodland edges and marsh edges. Access to water may be important; rarely found in very arid places.
range: Native to Asia and introduced to North America as a game bird. Established across southern Canada and much of the United States, thriving especially on the northern prairies; some populations are probably maintained by releases of game-farm birds.

lookalikes.name: Prairie grouse (e.g. sharp-tailed grouse)
lookalikes.howToTell: Audubon cautions that the brown female pheasant should be compared with prairie grouse; the pheasant hen has a much longer tail.
